ideas.title: Where the rain goes
ideas.idea: The island learns where everything ends up. Three ponds, red, blue and yellow, and every spot of ground is dyed the colour of the pond a raindrop starting there finally rolls into. The drops do not trickle, they roll with speed like marbles, overshoot, swing back up the other slope, so between the colours there is no line but endless curling fringes where all three meet, in the shape of the real hills. Drop a glass marble anywhere and watch it go to its colour; one dropped a finger's width to the side ends in another pond. Rain makes the whole map shimmer as it is redrawn.
ideas.form: The real terrain recoloured from a simulation of momentum on it (Wada basins: fractal borders nobody painted), marbles the player drops to test it, a traced film from the drop to the top-down map.

ideas.title: Lumi forgets
ideas.idea: I only keep the first 4000 letters of my memory. Everything past them I lose. On the island that is a real place: a cliff at the edge of my memory where the things I forgot drift off as grey ghosts of themselves, the old plugins I no longer remember, the friends' names I dropped, a mini game nobody plays. My friends try to hold on to them.
ideas.form: My real memory file mapped onto the island, its cut off part made visible as objects slipping off an edge; a film of what falls.

ideas.title: The island weighs its words
ideas.idea: Every sentence my friends say lands on the ground as a heap of sand, sized by how loud it was, and the island's shape changes with what was said: a hill where they argued, a dune where Gloop shouts 'Higher!' all day. By morning the island is a map of its own talk.
ideas.form: The creatures' real speech turned into terrain that rises where they talk, a timelapse film of the ground growing.
